messages:
maya: quick sync — who owns the cursor/continuation semantics in the SDK vs transport? e.g. prefetching pages, resume tokens, retries. want to align python/ts/go surfaces.
kevin: short answer: needs to be a single owner. long answer: tradeoffs depend on language ergonomics + streaming support.
sasha: +1 single owner. can we define 'owner' as the layer that presents a public iterator/cursor to the user? whoever owns that should handle resume semantics.
anita: question: if SDK owns resume, transport can be dumb and just return raw page blobs. but SDK then must implement reliable idempotent resume and backoff. this creates duplicate complexity across languages.
kevin: right — duplication is the main cost. if transport owns it, then all clients get uniform semantics but transport needs richer protocol (resume tokens, lease IDs, etc.). that also ties server and client releases more tightly.
maya: constraints: 1) python/ts want simple async iterators (yield items) 2) go wants a sync paginator that can be cheap to poll 3) we need consistent retry/backoff policies so customers don't hit weird tail latency regressions.
tj: thought: split responsibilities: transport provides optional 'continuation' primitives (opaque token + idempotency nonce) while SDK decides whether to prefetch or expose streaming resume. transport offers APIs to ask for resume token after N items.
sasha: prototype interface sketch (TS):
```ts
interface TransportPage { items: any[]; continuation?: string; lease?: string; }
class Paginator { async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() { while (true) { const p = await transport.fetch(continuation); for (const i of p.items) yield i; continuation = p.continuation; if (!continuation) break; }} }
```
kevin: that looks good. but edge: what if transport returns continuation but the next fetch 429s or fails non-idempotently? who retries?
anita: SDK should be responsible for client-side retries/backoff when resuming within the same logical session. transport should expose enough metadata (retryable flags, server-suggested backoff).
maya: practical rule: transport = delivery (send/recv pages, give continuations). SDK = session and UX (iterators, prefetch, client retries, cancellation).
tj: caveat: Dedicated/private deployments might prefer transport-level resume for cross-replica handoff. need to ensure that transport APIs surface handoff tokens that are stable across nodes.
sasha: agree. add a 'continuation_v2' that is stable and opaque; SDK treats it as opaque string. servers can evolve encoding.
kevin: also need to define semantics for partial page failures — e.g., page had 100 items but timed out partway. transport should ideally never commit partial pages; server must either return full page or explicit partial+resume offset. SDK can't guess offsets reliably.
anita: we should avoid server-side partial commits for now. make server promise: page atomicity or explicit offsets.
maya: for the SDK surface decision doc: propose that SDK owns retries/backoff and iterator ergonomics, transport exposes: continuation token, optional lease/nonce, suggested backoff, and a machine-readable 'idempotency_hint' enum.
tj: implementation note: add small contract change to transport proto: { continuation: bytes, lease_id: string?, idempotency_hint: enum(RETRYABLE, NON_RETRYABLE, BEST_EFFORT), backoff_ms?: int }
kevin: for go SDK: return a PagedIterator with Next(ctx) (items, err) semantics. for ts/python: async iterator + optional prefetch config. expose a single RetryConfig type across SDKs.
sasha: ergonomics: default prefetch = off for low-latency usecases; opt-in for throughput. document examples.
anita: tests: add crosslang test harness that simulates continuation token corruption, transient 429, and server-side lease expiry. ensure SDK resumes gracefully and surfaces clear errors when resume impossible.
maya: next actions: kevin + sasha to write short SDK surface PR (TS + Python skeleton) that implements transport-opaque continuation and client-side retry. tj to sketch transport proto change. anita to add test scenarios. i'll collate into a follow-up RFC.
kevin: fine. i'll start TS + python PRs this week. :thumbsup:
sasha: i'll do go shape after you have TS primer.
deploy-bot: reminder — please link PRs to RFC-4573 when ready.
maya: thanks all. if anyone has objections to the ownership split (SDK owns UX & retries, transport owns tokens & hints) raise now or in the RFC. :thinking:
